trigger: CPU-contention/scheduler delay between the calling thread and the detached GuardianIoExecutor worker delays on_disarm_complete() (the disarm's async completion callback) past the point where the test asserted completion counters immediately after detach_all()/detach_rule() returned
line: 5383, 5542 (at reviewed_at_sha 6ad301692 - the fix's new spin_until call sites; the flake itself raced on the CHECK/REQUIRE assertions immediately below these two lines, present since rung 9c PR-2 Unit 3 made detach_all()/detach_rule() dispatch disarms off-lock - parent 55c605293, the pre-fix sha the flake was reproduced against)
summary: Two PRE-EXISTING tests ('rung 9c R5.2: rapid attaches on distinct keys all commit...' ~line 5341, and the adversarial-review C1/K1' test 'a detach arriving right after the commit disarms the LIVE rule' ~line 5492) asserted disarm-completion counters (b->disarms.load()+rt->disarm_retained()==200; b->disarmed_ids().size()==1) immediately after detach_all()/detach_rule() returned. Rung 9c PR-2 Unit 3 (this same branch, already governance-passed in this run's earlier rounds) made both calls dispatch each key's disarm off-lock via submit_disarm_off_lock() and return once the disarm is ADMITTED, not once the backend call (running on a detached GuardianIoExecutor worker) physically completes via on_disarm_complete() - turning the immediate assertion into a race against that worker under CPU contention. Found by this session's own coordinator via a separate ASan-verification pass on this worktree - self-attributed, not an independent third-party review (independent_reporters stays 1 per the sec-1 lesson already corrected earlier in this ledger; the skill's own independence-is-asserted-not-enforced caveat applies). Reproduced deterministically under artificial load (stress-ng --cpu 32 --cpu-load 100, load average 25-44) against pre-fix code (parent 55c605293): test 1 failed 5/5 (196==200 each time), test 2 failed 4/5 (0==1). Fixed in 6ad301692 by inserting yuzu::test::spin_until(..., 10s) settles on the real completion signal before each assertion, matching this file's own pre-existing spin_until idiom (60+ other call sites); no sleep-based band-aid was added, and the CHECK/REQUIRE lines following each new settle are byte-identical to before (diff is purely additive, 19 lines). Reachability independently re-verified at 6ad301692 three ways, none of which surfaced a permanent-false or hang risk: (1) this session's own grep of guardian_spark_runtime.cpp confirms disarm_retained_ increments only at two sites (line 368 sync admission-refusal, line 409 on_disarm_complete WorkerThrew) and is NEVER decremented anywhere in the file, and redrive_retained_disarms() (the only function that could re-drive an already-counted claim) has NO production or test caller on this branch - so the 200-claim partition (disarms + disarm_retained()) cannot overshoot 200 or leave a permanent gap in this test; (2) quality-engineer and (3) cpp-safety each independently re-derived the same reachability proof at 6ad301692 (Gate 3 re-entry, 2026-09-13) and returned clean; cpp-expert confirmed the 19 added lines are idiomatic, race-free C++ (atomics + ids_mu_-guarded accessor for disarmed_ids(), [&] captures of TEST_CASE-scope-spanning shared_ptr locals, no lifetime issue). Empirically re-run: tests-build-agent-linux_x64/yuzu_agent_tests "[spark][runtime][liveness]" green (1161 assertions, 50 test cases) at 6ad301692 in this worktree. The three Gate 3 agents are closure evidence for the fix, not independent co-finders of the original flake.

trigger: redrive_retained_disarms() re-submits an already-counted Queued disarm claim via submit_disarm_off_lock(); if that redrive later succeeds, the claim's earlier disarm_retained_ increment (recorded when it was first refused, guardian_spark_runtime.cpp lines 368/409) is never decremented to compensate
summary: cpp-safety's Gate 3 re-entry reachability proof for the 6ad301692 settle-fix (flake-disarm-settle-r52, this ledger) surfaced a latent double-count hazard in PRE-EXISTING code (rung 9c PR-2 Unit 3/R5.2, already governance-passed in this run's earlier rounds, NOT touched by 6ad301692): redrive_retained_disarms() re-submits any Queued disarm claim, and disarm_retained_ is fetch_add-only throughout the file (grep confirmed - no decrement site exists), so a claim that is first retained-on-refusal and later successfully redriven would land in BOTH the disarms bucket and stay counted in disarm_retained_, breaking the 'strict partition of N claims' invariant this file's own qe-303 comment establishes. Today this is INERT: redrive_retained_disarms() has no production or test caller anywhere on this branch (grep confirmed independently by this session, cpp-expert, and quality-engineer) - it exists per its own comment for 'a future heartbeat tick (Unit 5)', so the hazard cannot fire yet and does not affect 6ad301692's correctness or either re-reviewed test's reachability. Checked against the existing open 'consistency-detach-all-comment' row in this same ledger (a missing-comment gap about detach_all()'s externally-invalidated-receipt contract) - no overlap, distinct concern. Recorded as a forward-looking NICE for whichever future unit wires redrive_retained_disarms() into a periodic caller: that caller must either decrement disarm_retained_ on a successful redrive or otherwise avoid re-counting the claim. trigger: on_arm_complete()'s compensating-disarm build assigned `cont = std::make_shared<ArmCompensation>()` before the also-fallible `cont->key = key` string copy; an ordinary allocation-class throw on the key copy alone (the SAME trigger class 27213156b was itself fixing for C1) leaves `cont` already non-null
summary: Gate 8 re-entry on 27213156b (fjarvis's C1 fix, PR #4318): cpp-safety and security-guardian, dispatched in parallel by workflow-orchestrator with a specific interleaving to verify (surfaced via an advisor consultation, then independently structurally confirmed by the orchestrator against source - ArmCompensation::key is std::string, genuinely fallible), each independently traced the actual code and confirmed a residual gap in the C1 fix itself. If make_shared<ArmCompensation>() succeeds but the very next statement, `cont->key = key`, throws, `cont` is already non-null (C++ does not retroactively unwind a completed prior statement). The catch handler calls direct_disarm_fallback(key, sub) once (disarm #1), but `if (cont)` below is then still true, so the full continuation branch ALSO runs, submitting a second backend->disarm(sub) for the same subscription (disarm #2). cpp-safety confirmed the double disarm is empirically reproducible (not just theoretical) and that SparkEngine::disarm() is id-idempotent with non-recycled ids on the shipped backend (spark_engine.cpp:1186, next_id_ at spark_engine.hpp:645) - the second disarm call is harmless in practice, but ISparkBackend::disarm() documents no such contract, and the test double (FakeBackend) does not dedupe. security-guardian traced the more severe downstream consequence: since std::string::operator= gives the strong exception guarantee, `cont->key` was left "" (never the real key) when the copy threw, so finalize_arm_compensation()'s claims_.find(cont->key) misses the real key entirely - the already-terminal head claim is never popped, and every sweep function that could otherwise rescue it (expire_overdue_claims, sweep_terminal_queued_locked, try_dispatch_head_locked) explicitly skips a claim in this state by design, so the key is PERMANENTLY WEDGED (no arm/disarm possible on it again short of a process restart) - a silent Guardian enforcement hole on the exact F3/on_arm_complete chokepoint the routed concern calls catastrophic-if-violated. Reachable on an ordinary internal allocation-failure path (E0, no actor, same trigger class as C1 itself). Both agents confirmed the new Unit 4 test (fault point 4, positioned before make_shared) does not exercise this interleaving (fault point 4 fires before the allocation even runs) and recommended the same minimal fix: build into a local and move into `cont` only after the full build succeeds, so `cont`'s nullity is atomic with the whole build.
